docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/proposals/prop-energy-nutrition-label.md:1041:| Linearity | Hold the prompt profile fixed and ramp the requested output from 128 to 2048 tokens. Regress gross request and decode energy on the runtime-observed output count; inspect residual structure as well as the fitted slope. | Energy responds proportionally over the tested dynamic range, and the fitted per-token slope can serve as the known-effect standard for floor probes on this stack. It would not establish linearity outside the tested range or on another stack. | **[PENDING WINDOW C]** |
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/proposals/prop-energy-nutrition-label.md:1042:| Null response across magnitudes | Run identical A-equals-B ABBA blocks at short, medium, and long output magnitudes. Evaluate the paired deltas against zero and against the predicted decision envelopes. | The comparison path does not create a directional effect merely because total energy or duration changes, and false contrasts across the tested range are contained by the error model. A non-significant result alone is insufficient; the interval must be interpreted relative to the floor. | **[PENDING WINDOW C]** |
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/proposals/prop-energy-nutrition-label.md:1043:| Empirical floor verification | Use the pre-registered linearity slope to create micro-deltas with predicted effects near 0.5, 1, 1.5, and 3 times the declared floor. Test positive and negative directions in counterbalanced blocks. | Sub-floor effects are refused while sufficiently super-floor effects clear in both directions. This is an operational check of the detection boundary, not a validation of the counter's absolute gain. | **[PENDING WINDOW C]** |
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/proposals/prop-energy-nutrition-label.md:1044:| Phase-attribution causal consistency | First compare the sum of separately integrated phase energies with the gross energy over their enclosing request. Then vary output length while holding prompt tokens fixed and fit the slope of prefill energy against output length. | Phase accounting is additive within its stated boundaries, and energy assigned to prefill does not acquire a systematic dependence on work that occurs later in decode. Together these tests challenge both missing energy and cross-phase leakage. | **[PENDING WINDOW C]** |
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/proposals/prop-energy-nutrition-label.md:1045:| Drift and settling | Place long controlled holds and fixed reference workloads through the window, including start, midpoint, and end references. After operator or stage activity, repeat the reference while recording the time required for thermal and admission observables to stabilize; compare it with the 180 s operating convention. | The measured drift trajectory is contained by the published allowance, and the chosen settling time is supported or revised from observed recovery rather than convenience. Endpoint agreement alone is not enough if the midpoint reveals curvature. | **[PENDING WINDOW C]** |
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/proposals/prop-energy-nutrition-label.md:1046:| Between-session stability | Repeat calibrations, null blocks, and floor cells across at least three sessions or days with the full stack identity recorded. | The calibration and floor are stable enough to reuse only under their declared freshness and identity rules, or reveal that a new session must mint a new floor. | **[PENDING WINDOW C]** |
docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/proposals/prop-energy-nutrition-label.md:1048:Linearity and the null ladder test complementary failure modes. A smooth response can still carry an offset, and a zero-centered null can coexist with a nonlinear scale. The micro-delta experiment then closes the loop by using the measured slope to place effects deliberately below and above the declared decision boundary. Success requires the instrument to refuse the former and resolve the latter in both directions; merely observing larger effects with larger workloads is not sufficient.

Impact: high (wrong deliverable built).</li> <li>Trigger: Phase 2 implementation slices ready to start (2A-2F complete) with P1-001 still open; or any supervisor communication contradicting <code>AGENT_PLAN.md</code> scope.</li> <li>Status note (2026-07-05): the first trigger fired 2026-06-12 (2A-2F completed with P1-001 still open). The mitigation is holding as designed - all work since has been hardware-independent and harness-shaped (mock slice, docs, Slice 2N is next and is also ungated) - and the fallback (&quot;continue only mock/local work; hardware purchases/borrows blocked-on-approval&quot;) is effectively in force.</li> <li>Mitigation: the queue keeps P1-001 ranked first; all work until approval stays hardware-independent and harness-shaped (valuable under any scope); the Phase 1 exit checklist lists the exact questions to put to the supervisor so one meeting can close the gate.</li> <li>Fallback: if approval stalls past mock-slice completion, continue only mock/local work and mark every hardware purchase or borrow decision blocked-on-approval.</li> <li>Owner: user.</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-002-powermetrics-sudo-workflow-not-approved-on-measurement-mac">R-002: powermetrics sudo workflow not approved on measurement Mac</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 2. Likelihood: low (user controls the machine; a local auth session needs rescheduling - the planned 2026-06-10 slot passed without one). Impact: high (no Mac telemetry = no flagship vertical slice).</li> <li>Status: closed-residual (2026-07-08). The working Mac slice completed 2G/2H/2I on 2026-07-06 with privileged powermetrics capture and strict-valid bundles; revisit for new macOS/MLX/powermetrics versions or new Mac hardware.</li> <li>Trigger: scoped sudoers rule (D-004) cannot be installed, or privileged sample capture fails after the auth session.</li> <li>Mitigation: D-004 defines a minimal, single-binary sudoers rule with the exact line documented in the Phase 1 exit checklist&#39;s instrumentation section; interactive-sudo manual fallback documented for attended runs.</li> <li>Fallback: attended runs with interactive sudo (operator present per experiment); if even that is unacceptable, the Mac becomes runtime-supported/telemetry-blocked and the first real slice moves to the first available CUDA target - recorded as a finding, not hidden.</li> <li>Owner: user (install rule), agent (pre-check + structured failure).</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-003-mlx-install-or-model-load-failure-on-mac">R-003: MLX install or model-load failure on Mac</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 2. Likelihood: low. Impact: medium (delays flagship slice).</li> <li>Status: closed-residual (2026-07-08). The working Mac slice completed 2G/2H/2I on 2026-07-06 with MLX generation and strict-valid bundles; revisit for new MLX/mlx-lm versions or new Mac hardware.</li> <li>Trigger: <code>pip install mlx mlx-lm</code> fails, or the chosen model (D-016) has no working MLX artifact.</li> <li>Mitigation: install into a dedicated venv with versions recorded in run bundles; model criteria (D-016) require known MLX availability before selection; smoke-test load before scheduling measurement sessions.</li> <li>Fallback: llama.cpp with the Metal backend as the Mac runtime (already a planned runtime for split portability under D-015); the MLX adapter then becomes optional rather than flagship.</li> <li>Owner: agent (with user approving installs).</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-004-kv-persist-resume-unsupported-in-a-target-runtime">R-004: KV persist/resume unsupported in a target runtime</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 3. Likelihood: medium overall (high for vLLM file-based replay, low for llama.cpp, low-medium for mlx-lm). Impact: high if unmitigated - this is the project&#39;s central feasibility risk.</li> <li>Trigger: a Stage 3.0 spike returns <code>replay_unsupported</code> for a runtime needed by a planned pairing.</li> <li>Mitigation: D-015&#39;s feasibility ladder - spikes run <em>before</em> any split hardware time is scheduled; pairings are planned only on runtimes with <code>replay_supported</code> verdicts; the synthetic transfer microbenchmark (Stage 3.1) is independent of all runtime cooperation and guarantees a crossover dataset.</li> <li>Fallback: analytical composition - measured prefill energy (node A) + measured synthetic transfer energy (payload sized by the KV model) + measured decode energy (node B) bounds the split cost honestly; the report states the composition method explicitly.</li> <li>Owner: agent.</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-005-llama-cpp-cache-files-not-portable-across-machines-backends">R-005: llama.cpp cache files not portable across machines/backends</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 3. Likelihood: medium (session files are version- and model-sensitive; cross-backend CUDA-save -&gt; Metal-load is unverified). Impact: high for <em>heterogeneous</em> pairings specifically.</li> <li>Trigger: Stage 3.0.2&#39;s cross-machine restore test fails or produces divergent output.</li> <li>Mitigation: the spike tests cross-machine restore explicitly, with pinned identical llama.cpp versions and identical GGUF files on both ends, before any heterogeneous experiment is scheduled.</li> <li>Fallback: restrict offline-replay pairings to same-platform pairs (GPU-&gt;GPU in the borrow window, Orin-&gt;Orin); cover heterogeneous pairs with the analytical composition (R-004 fallback); report the portability finding itself - it is a legitimate disaggregation-practicality result.</li> <li>Owner: agent.</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-006-3080-ti-borrow-window-slips-or-shrinks">R-006: 3080 Ti borrow window slips or shrinks</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 3. Likelihood: medium. Impact: medium (loses GPU-&gt;GPU pairing, not the phase).</li> <li>Trigger: window not scheduled by Phase 3 Stage 3.2 completion; or window arrives before split tooling is ready.</li> <li>Mitigation: all split tooling reaches rehearsed-on-available-hardware state before the window (the Phase 3 plan keeps a borrow-window runbook so borrow time is execution-only, no debugging); calendar mapping task (P1-008) makes the window a tracked date.</li> <li>Fallback: GPU-&gt;GPU pairing drops to single-GPU prefill/decode phase decomposition plus analytical composition; 3050&lt;-&gt;Orin and Orin&lt;-&gt;Orin remain.</li> <li>Owner: user (scheduling), agent (runbook readiness).</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-007-no-wall-meter-available">R-007: No wall meter available</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 1-4. Likelihood: medium. Impact: medium (boundary calibration and Pi/Hailo coverage lost; per-target results stand).</li> <li>Trigger: P1-003 resolves &quot;unavailable&quot;.</li> <li>Mitigation: P1-003 is a Phase 1 gate precisely so this resolves before it matters; D-018&#39;s boundary table makes results honest without a meter.</li> <li>Fallback: report within-target comparisons (always boundary-consistent) as primary; flag cross-target absolute comparisons with the boundary caveat; targets with no platform telemetry (Pi) become telemetry-unavailable findings.</li> <li>Owner: user.</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-008-orin-telemetry-inaccessible">R-008: Orin telemetry inaccessible</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 2-3. Likelihood: medium (rail sysfs paths vary by L4T version). Impact: low (one target of several).</li> <li>Trigger: P1-006 evidence shows neither INA3221 sysfs nor tegrastats usable.</li> <li>Mitigation: two candidate mechanisms documented before hardware time; wall-meter fallback if R-007 resolves positively.</li> <li>Fallback: Orin runs runtime-only (latency/throughput) marked telemetry-unavailable, or drops to a stretch target.</li> <li>Owner: user (access), agent (adapter).</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-009-hailo-cannot-run-llm-shaped-workloads">R-009: Hailo cannot run LLM-shaped workloads</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 1. Likelihood: high. Impact: low - <em>by design</em>: the plan treats Hailo as a feasibility investigation whose negative verdict is itself a reportable applicability finding.</li> <li>Status: <strong>realized as expected, 2026-06-12</strong> — verdict <code>unsupported_workload</code>. The trigger fired (a non-<code>supported</code> verdict), the by-design mitigation held, and the outcome is the publishable applicability finding the plan anticipated. No schedule impact.</li> <li>Trigger: feasibility checklist closes with any non-<code>supported</code> verdict. (Fired 2026-06-12.)</li> <li>Mitigation: none needed; the verdict-code structure in the Phase 1 exit checklist&#39;s Hailo section makes the outcome publishable either way. Do not spend implementation effort on a Hailo backend (the verdict is now recorded; the standing do-not-do-yet rule becomes &quot;report, don&#39;t implement&quot;).</li> <li>Fallback: Pi 5 CPU-only llama.cpp with wall-meter telemetry becomes an optional low-power data point if the meter exists; otherwise Pi/Hailo appears only in the applicability table.</li> <li>Owner: user (device access), agent (verdict documentation - done).</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-010-controller-as-dut-contamination-on-mac-runs">R-010: Controller-as-DUT contamination on Mac runs</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 2. Likelihood: high if unmitigated. Impact: medium (biased flagship numbers).</li> <li>Status: mitigated by D-013 (idle baseline includes resident quiescent controller; deferred logging; blocking wait during measured window).</li> <li>Trigger (residual): SSH-controlled comparison runs (once transport exists) show a delta beyond run-to-run variance.</li> <li>Fallback: move Mac headline measurements to remote-controlled runs.</li> <li>Owner: agent.</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-011-benchmark-network-cannot-be-isolated">R-011: Benchmark network cannot be isolated</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 3. Likelihood: medium (campus/home network constraints unknown until P1-004 closes). Impact: medium (noisy transfer measurements).</li> <li>Trigger: P1-004 topology answer shows shared links only.</li> <li>Mitigation: prefer direct node-to-node cabling (no switch) for 1GbE/2.5GbE point-to-point tests - removes the isolation question entirely for two-node experiments; record link conditions per run in the bundle.</li> <li>Fallback: run sweeps off-hours, repeat n&gt;=5, report observed throughput alongside nominal link speed (the bundle already records measured throughput per D-008&#39;s transfer block).</li> <li>Owner: user (hardware), agent (recording).</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-012-schedule-five-phases-vs-fixed-academic-deadlines">R-012: Schedule: five phases vs fixed academic deadlines</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: all. Likelihood: medium. Impact: high (capstones fail by calendar, not by code).</li> <li>Trigger: any phase exceeding its (to-be-set) calendar budget; colloquium or report dates announced (P1-008) leaving less runway than the plan assumes.</li> <li>Mitigation: P1-008 maps phases to real dates as soon as the user supplies them (<code>docs/milestones.md</code> holds the skeleton); every phase defines a hardware-independent floor and a descope ladder so cutting is a decision, not a scramble.</li> <li>Descope ladder (worst-case minimum viable capstone, in cut order):<ol> <li>Drop live split (3.3) - already stretch.</li> <li>Drop 10GbE and one model size.</li> <li>Drop heterogeneous replay pairs (keep synthetic transfer + analytical composition).</li> <li>Drop Orin/Pi targets (keep Mac + one CUDA).</li> <li>Floor: mock harness + Mac vertical slice + homogeneous baselines + synthetic interconnect sweep + analytical split model. This is still a complete, defensible benchmark-plus-study.</li> </ol> </li> <li>Owner: user (dates), agent (floor discipline).</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-013-thermal-throttling-confounds-measurements">R-013: Thermal throttling confounds measurements</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 2-4. Likelihood: medium (high on passively-cooled Orin/Pi). Impact: medium (rep-to-rep drift, biased late reps).</li> <li>Status: mitigated by D-014 (idle-power recovery gate between reps, thermal_drift_c in measurement quality, interleaved ordering) - residual risk on targets without thermal sensors.</li> <li>Trigger: thermal_drift_c trending across reps, or cooldown cap hits recorded in bundles.</li> <li>Fallback: longer cooldowns, active cooling notes recorded in run metadata, or excluding throttled reps <em>with documented cause</em> per D-014.</li> <li>Owner: agent.</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-014-model-weights-become-unavailable-or-gated">R-014: Model weights become unavailable or gated</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 2+. Likelihood: low. Impact: medium (mid-project model swap breaks comparability).</li> <li>Trigger: chosen model&#39;s hub entry gated/removed; license terms change.</li> <li>Mitigation: D-016 requires mirroring chosen weights to local storage immediately on selection, with revisions and hashes recorded.</li> <li>Fallback: promote the recorded fallback candidate; re-run affected baselines (the config hash separates old/new data cleanly).</li> <li>Owner: agent.</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-015-schema-changes-after-data-collection-starts">R-015: Schema changes after data collection starts</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 2+. Likelihood: low. Impact: high (existing bundles unreadable or silently misread).</li> <li>Status: mitigated structurally.</li> <li>Mitigation: schema_version field exists from v0.1; D-008 plans the only anticipated breaking-shape change (v0.2) <em>before</em> split data collection; output-schema additions are additive-only (the JSON schema does not forbid additional properties); <code>validate-bundle</code> pins what a valid bundle means per version.</li> <li>Trigger: any proposed non-additive change to a schema with bundles already on disk.</li> <li>Fallback: a dated migration note in this repo plus a one-shot migration script; never edit bundles in place (they are evidence).</li> <li>Owner: agent.</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-016-measurement-corpus-loss-runs-has-no-backup-path">R-016: Measurement-corpus loss (runs/ has no backup path)</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 2-5. Likelihood: low. Impact: high (the dataset behind every claim is a gitignored directory on one disk; a disk failure or an errant delete erases the evidence the defense rests on, and hardware re-collection needs access windows that may not recur).</li> <li>Trigger: first real (non-mock) bundle written; any data-affecting incident (disk error, iCloud eviction anomaly, accidental delete).</li> <li>Mitigation: before the first real measurement session (gate on 2I data collection, tracked as queue task P0-002), define and record the backup protocol here: destination (external disk and/or cloud location outside the repo), cadence (after every measurement session), method (rsync of <code>runs/</code> plus experiment manifests), and a restore test performed once. Configs + manifests already make re-collection well-defined; backups make it unnecessary.</li> <li><strong>Protocol recorded (2026-07-06, P0-002 closed interim).</strong> Destination: <code>~/JouleWise-backup</code> — a user-directed INTERIM location on the same disk (&quot;cursory... I&#39;ll handle that later&quot;); it protects against errant deletes but not disk failure, so the user still owes an external/cloud destination for full mitigation. Cadence: after every measurement session. Method: <code>scripts/backup_runs.sh [RUNS_DIR] [DEST]</code> (rsync -a, never <code>--delete</code>; dated UTC log line per invocation appended to <code>DEST/backup.log</code>). Restore test performed 2026-07-06: mock bundle backed up, restored to a temp dir, <code>validate-bundle</code> green on the restored copy. Swapping in the final destination is a one-argument change (or edit the script default) plus one fresh restore test.</li> <li><strong>Protocol upgraded (2026-07-10/11, P0-003 closed; addendum 2026-07-16 closing a summary-row/body drift found by the resumption audit).</strong> The interim same-disk destination above is superseded: the external destination is iCloud Drive, live with a fresh backup + restore test passed (evidence: <code>docs/run_reports/2026-07-11-c028-continuation.md</code> §11, &quot;The P0-003 iCloud measurement-corpus backup and restore gate is satisfied&quot;). The 2026-07-06 entry above is retained as history. Standing caveat: iCloud eviction — re-verify the destination is materialized (fresh restore test) before each measurement window.</li> <li>Fallback: re-run affected experiments from their configs (the config hash separates old/new data cleanly per D-005/D-010); report any unrecoverable gap honestly in the exclusion log.</li> <li>Owner: user (destination/media), agent (protocol doc + restore test).</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-017-repo-lives-on-icloud-synced-desktop-eperm-lock-recurrence">R-017: Repo lives on iCloud-synced Desktop (EPERM lock recurrence)</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: all. Likelihood: low (mitigated; was high while on Desktop). Impact: medium (blocks work sessions mid-run; small integrity risk around eviction during writes).</li> <li>Status: <strong>mitigated 2026-07-05</strong> - the repo moved off the synced Desktop (current canonical path: <code>~/code/JouleWise</code>; the interim <code>~/code/CapstoneRivoire/Capstone</code> path recorded here was itself later renamed - corrected 2026-07-09, C-027). P0-001 complete; git + suite verified green at the new path. Residual exposure: agent sessions launched from the stale Desktop path (delete the leftover <code>~/Desktop/CapstoneRivoire</code> husk after relaunching from the new path), and any future placement of repo or <code>runs/</code> data under an iCloud-synced directory - do not.</li> <li>Trigger: any <code>Operation not permitted</code> on read/readdir inside the repo with the iCloud file provider (<code>bird</code>) active.</li> <li>History: first incident 2026-06-12 (documented in <code>RUN_STATE.md</code>); recurred 2026-07-05 mid-run - <code>docs/</code>, <code>joulewise/</code>, <code>tests/</code>, <code>.git</code>, and the repo root EPERM-locked intermittently during an active iCloud full-sync, clearing and re-locking per subtree. Both incidents match iCloud &quot;Optimize Mac Storage&quot; behavior on <code>~/Desktop/</code>. The move landed the same day as the second incident.</li> <li>Fallback: if a lock ever strikes again, wait for it to clear (both incidents did), then re-verify with the test suite before continuing; the remote (<code>origin/main</code>) bounds code loss to the working tree.</li> <li>Owner: user (launch paths), agent (post-lock verification discipline).</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-018-the-agent-loop-itself-as-a-schedule-and-scope-risk">R-018: The agent loop itself as a schedule and scope risk</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: all. Likelihood: medium. Impact: high (capstones fail by calendar, R-012).</li> <li>Registered by C-027 (NEGSPACE lens finding accepted in council): the multi-agent workflow can remain locally productive - packs, registries, meta-process, site work - while the graded deliverable path (rubric, report source, backup, real corpus, figures) stays starved. Same-day evidence at registration: ~6M tokens of breadth work vs six real corpus bundles, no report source, same-disk backup.</li> <li>Trigger: an agent-heavy work block that produces neither a new real evidence bundle nor a report/figure increment.</li> <li>Mitigation: D-060 depth-before-breadth stop line (RATIFIED by Ed 2026-07-10) extended by the WO-022/R2 spend guardrails (<code>docs/orchestration.md</code> §Spend guardrails, 2026-07-15); RPT-001 vertical slice; the C-027 correctness rows ranked ahead of all breadth work.</li> <li>Owner: lead (queue discipline + guardrail checkpoints), Ed (HARD bands and structure).</li> </ul> </div> </div> </main> <footer class="site"> <div class="inner"> <span>JouleWise · github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</span> <span>docs/risk_register.md · commit dbd8137 · regenerate: <span class="mono">python3 scripts/build_site.py</span></span> </div> </footer> </body> </html>

class="doc-meta"><a href="library.html">Back to sources</a> · rendered from <code>TASK_QUEUE.md</code></p> <div class="provenance-plate"><span class="source-chip" title="TASK_QUEUE.md · commit de665ea"><span class="source-file">TASK_QUEUE.md</span><span class="source-commit">commit de665ea</span></span></div> <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>JouleWise Task Queue</h1> <p>This is the live queue for JouleWise work. When the user gives a new task, first triage it here instead of assuming it should happen immediately.</p> <h2 id="intake-rule-for-new-tasks">Intake Rule For New Tasks</h2> <p>For every new user task:</p> <ol> <li>Read <code>RUN_STATE.md</code>.</li> <li>Read this file.</li> <li>Check <code>git status --short --branch</code>.</li> <li>Review the last 2-3 commits with <code>git log --oneline --decorate -3</code>.</li> <li>Check relevant handoffs in <code>docs/run_reports/</code>.</li> <li>If <code>RUN_STATE.md</code> contains an ACTIVE <code>ACTIVE_STOP_CARD</code>, that card outranks this queue. Execute or preserve the card&#39;s resume/cleanup instructions before considering any lower-ranked work.</li> <li>Decide whether the task is:<ul> <li>urgent workspace hygiene,</li> <li>Phase 1 evidence work,</li> <li>Phase 2 implementation prep,</li> <li>later-phase research work,</li> <li>documentation/reporting,</li> <li>or unrelated/new scope.</li> </ul> </li> <li>Place or update the task in the queue with priority, rationale, evidence, and blockers.</li> <li>If executing it now, say why it outranks the current top task.</li> <li>Closure rule (D-023): a row may move to Completed only after the corresponding phase exit-checklist matrix row already shows the same status with dated evidence, and the Completed row&#39;s evidence cell must cite that matrix row (file + item id). If no matrix row exists for the work, say so explicitly in the evidence cell.</li> </ol> <h2 id="priority-scale">Priority Scale</h2> <ul> <li><strong>P0 Safety</strong>: prevents accidental data loss, bad commits, broken handoffs, or corrupted repo state.</li> <li><strong>P1 Phase Gate</strong>: required to close the current phase or unblock the next phase responsibly.</li> <li><strong>P2 Next Slice</strong>: next implementation slice after current phase gates are adequately planned or closed.</li> <li><strong>P3 Research Expansion</strong>: useful experiment or feature, but not needed for current gate.</li> <li><strong>P4 Polish</strong>: quality-of-life, dashboard polish, formatting, cleanup, or presentation work.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ranking-factors">Ranking Factors</h2> <p>Rank higher when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Prevents accidental loss or bad Git history.</li> <li>Produces evidence for the current phase exit checklist.</li> <li>Removes ambiguity for multiple later steps.</li> <li>Is required before physical hardware time is spent.</li> <li>Is cheap to verify and reduces future confusion.</li> <li>Matches the current phase better than jumping ahead.</li> </ul> <p>Rank lower when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Depends on unavailable hardware or supervisor input.</li> <li>Is a later-phase feature.</li> <li>Adds polish before a runnable vertical slice exists.</li> <li>Produces code without a clear run-bundle or test artifact.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ready-shelf-rule">Ready/Shelf Rule</h2> <p>A partially built or proposed task is <strong>READY</strong> only when it has:</p> <ul> <li>one authority document or stream-log pointer,</li> <li>bounded files/modules or a bounded artifact target,</li> <li>explicit acceptance evidence or a verification command,</li> <li>no hidden hardware/user/token-budget dependency, and</li> <li>a named lane (<code>[AGENT]</code>, <code>[QUIET-MAC]</code>, or <code>[ED-EXTERNAL]</code>).</li> </ul> <p>If any of those are missing, keep the item as a shelved concept or planning note instead of letting it compete with executable queue work. Half-finished work should be resumed only through its authority pointer and stop-card/checkpoint state, not by inference from prose summaries.</p> <h2 id="machine-state-lanes-adopted-c-007-2026-07-07">Machine-State Lanes (adopted C-007, 2026-07-07)</h2> <p>Every task carries a lane; a session picks the top task COMPATIBLE with its machine state, not the top task absolutely:</p> <ul> <li><strong>[QUIET-MAC]</strong> — measurement campaigns only: no agent fleet, no Codex load, idle gate will flag contamination.</li> <li><strong>[AGENT]</strong> — code, docs, feasibility spikes; safe during agent-heavy sessions.</li> <li><strong>[ED-EXTERNAL]</strong> — needs the user: advisor, calendar, device access, purchases, destinations.</li> </ul> <h2 id="historical-queue-snapshot-superseded-2026-07-15">Historical Queue Snapshot (superseded 2026-07-15)</h2> <p>The former hand-authored live table was removed because it duplicated kernel tasks. <strong>A1 terminal-mock-bar gap — the session&#39;s best catch</strong>: an <em>honest</em> mock member could reach claim evidence with all mock-exempted barriers disabled, no attacker required; the NEG-8 sentinel route on round-3 F2 (the one route with no downstream catch); and the F3 fixture-fix refutation (a production-promoted fixture cannot be strict-valid — use a patch idiom instead).</li> <li><strong>Sol-execution refuter (unique):</strong> discovery of the coordinated-downgrade <em>variants</em> (strip the drift group and restore the headline floors and the record validates clean — reproduced on the repo fixture, gate <code>20.799350577898302 → 20.399350577898304</code>, exactly the fixture&#39;s 0.4 J allowance; asymmetric removal from the comparative record alone also validates clean); the G2A adjacent blocker (the reduce layer independently trusts metadata/summary mockness in the environment and CPU-admission barriers, so fresh re-reduction reproduces the forged exemption and strict stored-vs-fresh comparison is not a backstop); identification of the authoritative mockness source (custody-bound <code>config().hardware_target.telemetry_backend</code>, bound through <code>metadata.config_sha256</code>); the <code>mock:*</code> tagged-source class caveat (<code>axi_valid_burst</code> config <code>mock</code> vs summary <code>mock:target</code> — compare backend <em>class</em>, not raw strings); and every runnable probe, including the estimand-flip demonstration (<code>mock</code> → no refusals vs <code>powermetrics</code> → <code>whole_window_verdict_provenance_invalid</code> on identical evidence).</li> <li><strong>Lead (unique):</strong> the two D-078 clause-10 registry addenda (2 and 3) — component-7 anchor-fallback gate ruling derived from the a7-vs-a5 prefill-scatter root cause (a7&#39;s 11.85 J &quot;floor&quot; was one fallback-anchored member, r03; true floor ≈ 3.3–3.7 J), and the terminal mock bar; severity synthesis on the split verdicts (kept F4 at blocker priority on imminent-use grounds against the contract refuter&#39;s downgrade); the capsule shard-budget trim (<code>a5a7acf</code>) and the pagination ruling that followed (deterministic <code>D-NNN</code> pagination + D-076 artifact-cap redirects); the battery-flake adjudications; and the bench fixes (registry clause, the fixture metadata line that blocked Sol&#39;s canonical run, the round-4 assertion restore).</li> </ul> <p>Rough spend (estimates, not billing truth): the gauntlet proper (audit round 1 onward) recorded 11 distinct Sol wrapper invocations — 4 audits (3 xhigh, 1 high), 2 execution refuters (both high), 3 implementation rounds (xhigh; xhigh + a high alignment pass; high), 1 capsule session (xhigh), plus retry attempts on two of them; counting the same day&#39;s pre-audit wave, fold, fold2 and run-book sessions brings the day&#39;s Sol total to ~15. Four Opus agents: three contract/design refuters (~96k / 120k / 144k tokens) plus one dictated-fills drafting/verification agent (~115k) — the latter caught five material errors in the lead&#39;s own dictation of this entry, including the effort-tier discrepancy ruled on below. Lead orchestration on top. The <code>codex-usage</code> ledger reads all zeros for the 5h and 24h windows (&quot;local quota signal unavailable in referenced session logs&quot;) — the feed is suspected broken, so no token-volume snapshot is recorded this session.</p> <p>Verdict: <strong>the Opus-contract + Sol-execution pairing changed the triage outcome in every round it ran</strong> — it collapsed one blocker outright (F2), re-priced two (G1, G2), refuted two proposed fixes before they landed (G2 fixture, F3 fixture), and produced one blocker the auditor never saw (A1 terminal mock bar). The two lenses split on G1/G2 (Sol sustained both at blocker; Opus re-priced both) and the lead synthesized rather than majority-voted, per §C-028. Adopted as the default blocker-refuter shape; memory and skills to be updated by the lead.</p> <p>Dissent recorded: on F4 the lead overrode the contract refuter&#39;s downgrade and kept blocker priority, on the grounds that the anchor-fallback replay path was about to be exercised by the next window&#39;s re-verdict. On G1/G2 the lead implemented both fixes despite the contract lens&#39;s re-price, treating the re-price as a scope argument (what is <em>newly</em> broken) rather than a licence to defer.</p> <p>Calibration note: the auditor layer&#39;s yield is real but its severity calibration is not — four consecutive rounds produced findings worth fixing while its blocker tier held at roughly half strength. The refuter tier is what converts that into correct triage; running a single-lens refuter would have inherited the inflation.</p> <p>Effort-tier ruling (lead, flagged by the drafting agent&#39;s verification pass): the execution refuters ran at <code>high</code>, not the adversarial-review skill&#39;s <code>xhigh</code> default — deliberately in round 1 (Ed&#39;s A/B spec named &quot;sol high&quot;) and carried into round 2 for comparability. The A/B verdict therefore stands on high-tier refuters, which is the STRONGER form of the result: paired distinct-lens refuters at high changed triage outcomes that single-lens xhigh refuters have historically missed. Ruling: in the paired-lens shape, <code>high</code> is the default refuter tier; reserve <code>xhigh</code> for single-refuter verification or judgment-dense standalone audits. The lead will amend the adversarial-review skill&#39;s effort note accordingly.</p> <p>Scorecard (dispositions per docs/orchestration.md): 20 findings raised across 4 audit rounds incl. refuter adjacents. Accepted-and-fixed in PR #85: 13 (r1 F1/F3/F4/F5/F7; r2 G1/G2/G3 + adjacent A1 terminal mock bar; r3 F1/F2/F3; r4 F1). Re-priced by refuters before fixing: 4 of those (r1 F4 blocker→should-fix; r2 G1/G2 blocker→should-fix; r1 F2 blocker→docs-only, landed as contract clarification). Rejected / non-obligating: 2 (r1 F6 contract-refuted; r2-A2 traced not-reachable, defensive comment only). Queued: 4 → kernel row CUSTODY-HARDEN-01 (G2A reduce-layer label trust, drift-bound seal authentication, dead no-freshness accommodation, artifact_schema_invalid mislabel); full-strip custody discrimination remains inside pre-existing FLOOR-BIND-01/L1. Owners: all fixed items closed at merge c3e2647 (lead-verified); queued items owned by the kernel rows named above; no open finding without an owner.</p> </div> </div> </main> <footer class="site"> <div class="inner"> <span>JouleWise · github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</span> <span>docs/council_log.md · commit 1af9f92 · regenerate: <span class="mono">python3 scripts/build_site.py</span></span> </div> </footer> </body> </html>
docs/process_traces/2026-08-07-night-hardening/AUDIT-RUNNER.md:15883:docs/process_traces/2026-07-17-extension-axes/axes-evaluations.json:78:  "summary": "The literal NVIDIA-vs-AMD question is out of reach for this capstone: the D-073 fleet is a 128 GB M3 Max plus a 3080 Ti (12 GiB), Jetson optional replication only, and no AMD hardware exists or is planned; D-070 caps every axis at L2 as a stress test of the single Q4 thesis. The honest within-fleet reductions of this axis already have registry homes: C5-2.7 is exactly \"same llama.cpp build/model/quant across devices with the runtime variable removed\" (the portable-kernel-runtime-as-controlled-variable design, bank line ~865), C5-1.8 is same-machine cross-runtime energy attribution (bank line ~668), and C5-3.3 already holds the cross-ISA/AMD platform question as hardware-gated L4-after-replication. What the axis genuinely adds is not a new askable question but an explanatory variable: kernel-layer identity (attention kernel, BLAS/GEMM backend, Triton-vs-handwritten, graph/capture mode), which today is only best-effort adapter metadata (\"Kernel/library where known\" row of the stack-identity table maps to metadata.adapters.runtime.prepare_metadata \"when captured\"). Both within-reach designs are partially confounded — the Metal-vs-CUDA llama.cpp comparison carries a device+measurement-boundary confound (powermetrics SoC rails vs nvidia-smi board power; per-boundary claims only until wall-calibrated per C5-2.9), and the same-silicon 3080 Ti cross-runtime comparison is stack-vs-stack when artifact formats differ, exactly as C5-1.8's methodology note already caps it. Verdict: this is predominantly a post-capstone platform question; the capstone-reach content is (a) a cheap kernel-provenance rider on C5-2.7/C5-1.8 and (b) minimal backend-provenance fields so bundles recorded now stay comparable if an AMD/ROCm leg arrives later under C5-3.3. A Sol high-effort read-only confirmation session was still in flight at the reporting deadline (audit trail: /Users/edr/code/JouleWise/.codex-bridge/20260717T071715Z-83677-new.*, session 019f6eef-c802-78a3-9629-c44baaf4c293); all repo claims here are lead-verified directly against the files cited.",

docs/process_traces/2026-08-07-night-hardening/AUDIT-MINT.md:14:NIGHT-STRANDER BUG HUNT, LENS 3 of 3: EXTRACTION + MINT + VERDICT CONSUMPTION PATH (read-only; write no files; final message = report, severity + file:line + concrete failing scenario each). Context: after each of three fresh quiet windows (decision D-117, end of docs/decision_log.md), the morning desk path runs: whole-window verdict -> governed extraction (extraction specs like configs/floor_mint/a10_extraction_spec.json) -> generalized floor mint embedding the never-zero allowance max(observed_drift_s, 0.010818) -> claims consumption. Known constraint: the mint historically had a HARD-CODED literal 7.377086 (D-084 era) that refuses any other value — locate the current pinset mechanism and report exactly what per-plan pin supply the generalized path expects, and whether a fresh window's mint can succeed today or what code changes remain. Also hunt: extraction spec validation gaps, evidence_root_id pin handling for NEW roots, verdict-to-extraction membership binding, allowance arithmetic, float formatting/rounding traps in six-decimal literals. A window whose data is perfect but whose morning mint REFUSES on tooling grounds is a lost night for the paper - rank findings by that risk.

docs/process_traces/2026-08-07-night-hardening/AUDIT-MINT.md:4034:./docs/site/adapter_contracts.html:48:</code></pre> <p>Only the reducer may assign <code>below_floor</code>; <code>excluded_from_claim</code> is analysis-only and invalid in runtime events or summaries (D-045.4).</p> <p>Prompt-source handling is per item and mutually exclusive. <code>prompt_text</code> is encoded at generation time with adapter-normal special-token behavior (MLX uses <code>add_special_tokens=True</code>, so BOS is inside the planned prompt budget). <code>prompt_token_ids</code> is ids-native and delivered exactly as listed, with no BOS added; this is required for D-046 sentinel conditions. Absent text and ids use a synthetic prompt with <code>shape.planned_prompt_tokens</code>. Any field named <code>prompt_sha256</code> means the domain-separated token-ID hash, not a text hash.</p> <p>For prompt-text items with a SHA-256-shaped <code>source.source_sha256</code>, runtimes compare the realized prompt token-ID hash against <code>source_sha256</code>; if it does not match, they may accept <code>sha256(prompt_text)</code> as a text-domain manifest. Any other value fails the item closed as <code>malformed</code> with <code>status_reason: &quot;prompt_ids_mismatch&quot;</code>. For planned prompt token counts, <code>jw_mixed_v1</code> prompt-text items are budgeted and a realized/planned mismatch is fatal; affine ladder prompt-text items are nominal and receive an advisory annotation instead.</p> <p><code>suite_items.jsonl.prompt_source</code> is one of <code>prompt_text</code>, <code>token_ids</code>, or <code>synthetic</code>. <code>bos_present</code> records whether BOS is present in the realized prompt. For text-path adapters, when the tokenizer exposes a BOS id this is <code>add_special_tokens=True</code> and first realized id equals the tokenizer BOS id; when the tokenizer does not expose BOS identity, <code>bos_present</code> records the honest encode-mode proxy (<code>add_special_tokens=True</code>). Ids-native and synthetic suite prompts record <code>false</code> unless a future adapter explicitly materializes BOS as part of those sources.</p> <h2 id="telemetry-adapter">Telemetry Adapter</h2> <p>Telemetry answers how power and thermal state are measured.</p> <p>Required behavior:</p> <ul> <li>Report device metadata, including the rail manifest: the exact rail names whose per-timestamp sum defines the backend&#39;s canonical <code>power_w</code> (D-018). Rail manifest entries are strings; non-string entries are rejected by the bundle reader rather than coerced.</li> <li>Measure idle baseline.</li> <li>Start power sampling.</li> <li>Stop power sampling.</li> <li>Emit raw power samples.</li> <li>Report thermal state when available.</li> <li>Return structured failure if telemetry permission is missing.</li> </ul> <p>Rail-row timestamp contract (D-027, Slice 2N.4): one sample instant is one clock read, fanned out to one row per manifest rail, all carrying that instant&#39;s single <code>timestamp_s</code>. A manifest rail may appear at most once for a given timestamp; duplicate <code>(timestamp_s, rail)</code> rows are invalid, including single-rail manifests. With a multi-rail manifest, a timestamp carrying only a subset of the manifest rails is a misalignment: the shared bundle reader raises a structured failure (the reducer reports FAILED; the report omits the chart) and default bundle validation reports the same trace-policy problem rather than silently producing an interleaved, undersummed, or double-counted curve. An adapter whose hardware samples rails at genuinely different instants must resample/align to shared timestamps before emitting rows - alignment policy belongs to the adapter that knows its hardware.</p> <p>Powermetrics NUL-framed plist parsing is lenient only for the final unparseable frame, and only after at least one complete frame parsed successfully. The adapter preserves the raw plist verbatim, drops that final frame only from derived parsing (<code>power_trace.csv</code> and rich telemetry), and records a non-gating <code>metadata.device.parse_diagnostics[]</code> entry describing the dropped tail. A midstream unparseable frame, or a capture with no complete frames, is still a hard parse failure.</p> <p>Mock telemetry sampling convention (D-019): for any nonzero <code>start_sampling</code>/<code>stop_sampling</code> span, <code>MockTelemetryAdapter</code> stamps synthetic measured samples strictly inside that adapter span, never at the boundary clock reads. It uses a centered nominal-period grid at the configured <code>sampling.power_hz</code>; if that would produce fewer than two samples, it emits two evenly spaced interior samples instead. This preserves deterministic constant-power math while ensuring the controller&#39;s post-start/pre-stop measured markers contain enough samples for reducer integration under both fake and real clocks.</p> <p>Initial telemetry backends:</p> <ul> <li><code>mock</code></li> <li><code>powermetrics</code></li> <li><code>nvidia_smi</code></li> <li><code>jetson_rails</code></li> <li><code>wall_meter</code></li> </ul> <h2 id="idle-admission-core-policy-extension-t0-5-audit-p1-1-p1-2-additive">Idle-Admission Core Policy Extension (T0.5, audit P1.1/P1.2; additive)</h2> <p>GPU-idle-only admission is no longer sufficient. The pure evaluators in <code>joulewise/idle_admission.py</code> add three fail-closed surfaces, driven by an additive campaign-policy sidecar section keyed <code>idle_admission_extension</code> (schema <code>joulewise.idle_admission_extension.v1</code>):</p> <ul> <li><p><strong>CPU-aware idle admission</strong>: policy-configurable criteria over the pre-run baseline rich telemetry (<code>rich_telemetry_idle.jsonl</code>) - nearest-rank p95 of the per-record max per-CPU busy ratio (<code>1 - idle_ratio - down_ratio</code>, clamped, so parked CPUs never read as busy) against <code>cpu_criteria.cpu_busy_ratio_p95_max</code>, and p95 of <code>processor_combined_power_w</code> against <code>cpu_criteria.processor_combined_power_w_p95_max</code>, with at least <code>cpu_criteria.min_samples</code> records. Admission requires the existing GPU-idle admission AND these criteria. Missing, malformed, or insufficient telemetry FAILS CLOSED when <code>cpu_criteria.on_missing_telemetry</code> is <code>fail</code> (mandatory for a production profile); an exploratory policy may use <code>flag</code> but must set <code>claim_bearing: false</code> (explicitly non-claim-bearing).</p> </li> <li><p><strong>Adapter-wattage continuity</strong>: <code>collect_environment_guard_observation</code> records the adapter surface (<code>power.adapter_watts</code>, <code>power.adapter_description</code>, plus a normalized <code>adapter_power_observation</code>) per admission observation when called with <code>include_adapter_power=True</code> (default off so pre-hookup callers keep their exact probe sequence AND their exact observation shape; the controller hookup opts in). Under the default flag the <code>power</code> block and <code>adapter_power_observation</code> keys are ABSENT entirely - not present as all-None placeholders - so the verdict&#39;s continuity scan (which treats any guard observation carrying a <code>power</code> key as an adapter observation) never ingests unverifiable unknown-wattage placeholders from callers that did not opt in. The campaign verdict evaluates the ordered observation sequence: wattage discontinuities (the live 140-&gt;70-&gt;140 W negotiation precedent) and description/power-source changes are NAMED conditions - recorded data, never a silent pass and never an implicit abort. Unknown adapter wattage fails closed when <code>adapter_wattage.require_known_wattage</code> is true (mandatory for production); stable known wattage passes.</p> </li> <li><p><strong>Prospective NEG-8 SCREEN + BUDGET</strong> — <strong>Ed-ratified 2026-07-24, superseding the prior gross-only amendment:</strong> the screen is claim-family aligned. It independently gates gross and idle-subtracted point drift against distinct bounds derived from the same named, settled, same-condition <code>n &gt;= 10</code> corpus. The hash-sealed <code>joulewise.neg8_drift_bound.v1</code> artifact records both families. For legacy one-member endpoints, <code>d054_point_contrast_guard_v1</code> remains <code>max(sample_range_j, t_0.975,n-1 * s * sqrt(2))</code>. Prospective endpoints are three members each: the screen uses the start/end endpoint means, records their standard errors, and compares the absolute mean delta (not a second SEM-inflated margin) to <code>max(mean(largest_3)-mean(smallest_3), t_0.975,n-1 * s * sqrt(2/3))</code>. The extreme-triplet term retains the largest corpus-supported endpoint-mean contrast; the Student-t term predicts two new three-member endpoint means. Recording SEM without adding it again avoids double-counting repeatability already represented by the bound. Gross envelope corners remain diagnostics only.</p> <p>Every evaluated window also mints a strictly positive allowance per family: <code>max(max(start_mean,midpoint,end_mean)-min(...), derived_bound)</code>. One midpoint member is mandatory for the prospective 3+1+3 protocol, so a non-monotone interior excursion cannot disappear behind similar endpoints. No duration multiplier is applied: the settled corpus identifies repeatability, not a drift-per-time law, and inventing linear physics would be less defensible than the observed trajectory maximum. The verdict records the no-scaling decision, member counts/means/SEMs, midpoint, excursion, selected bound, allowance, and derivation hash. Floor records add the family-matched allowance after the guarded/corner-widened floor; validation recomputes the sum and claim consumption uses both the drift-widened floor and the named deterministic allowance term.</p> <p>Missing/invalid family evidence refuses distinctly: <code>neg8_drift_bound_underived</code> (gross) and <code>neg8_idle_sub_drift_bound_underived</code> (idle-subtracted); both spellings are Ed-ratified D-078 registry additions. Family failures retain <code>neg8_bracket_abs_delta_exceeded</code> for gross and add <code>neg8_bracket_idle_sub_abs_delta_exceeded</code> for idle-subtracted. A delta exactly on its bound passes. The v1 sidecar&#39;s <code>max_abs_delta_j</code>/<code>max_rel_delta</code> remain legacy transport fields and do not gate amended rows.</p> <p><strong>BOUND FRESHNESS addendum — Ed-ratified 2026-07-24:</strong> the same sealed artifact carries <code>freshness.derived_at_s</code>, a fixed 24-hour <code>max_age_s = 86400</code>, and exact OS-build, power-supply-identity, and calibration-artifact-identity bindings. Twenty-four hours mirrors the governed instrument-calibration horizon: it permits one controlled measurement day without treating repeatability as indefinitely transferable. Evaluation records its timestamp, expiry, artifact and observed bindings, binding-resolution status, and every triggered re-derivation reason. Horizon expiry, OS build change, power-supply change, calibration identity change, or unresolved current binding makes both family bounds stale and refuses with the registered <code>neg8_drift_bound_stale</code>. A v1 artifact with an authentic pre-addendum seal but no freshness block is replay-readable only to produce that stale refusal; it is never grandfathered. Malformed or unsealed artifacts remain underived under the two family-specific spellings. The superseded pre-SCREEN+BUDGET gross-only v1 shape (no <code>claim_family_bounds</code>) is not replayable and refuses as malformed/underived; &quot;pre-addendum replay&quot; applies only to the dual-family shape with <code>claim_family_bounds</code> present and freshness absent.</p> <p>The bracket is a WHOLE-WINDOW check: the evaluated basis must contain both endpoints. Legacy pair-only windows (a5-a8) remain evaluable as 1+0+1: both families screen and each allowance is <code>max(abs(delta), bound)</code>. Replicated endpoints plus midpoint apply prospectively; existing basis-scoped legacy verdict rows retain their frozen interpretation. Per-segment invocations with only one endpoint (or neither) record <code>neg8_bracket_not_evaluated</code>, never a spurious missing/failure. A reference genuinely absent from an explicit whole-window pass still fails closed.</p> </li> </ul> <p>Verdict surface: <code>scripts/run_campaign.py</code> records the additive <code>idle_admission_core</code> section (schema <code>joulewise.idle_admission_core_verdict.v1</code>) on the campaign verdict with per-member CPU-admission results, the continuity result, the bracket result, and the union of named conditions. A sidecar without the extension yields the named condition <code>idle_admission_extension_unconfigured</code>.</p> <p>Hash/version enforcement: the campaign policy binding hash is the sha256 of the full sidecar bytes, extension included - changing any new field changes the policy identity; the extension additionally records its own canonical-JSON sha256 and requires exact schema/policy version strings and exact keys (unknown or missing keys are rejected).</p> <p>Deployment note (C2 hookup complete): <code>CampaignPolicy.from_mapping</code> now owns the typed additive extension parse, including profile-dependent fail-closed validation, so controller child runs re-parse the full hash-bound sidecar without a runner-side strip/parse workaround. The tracked production and exploratory sidecars carry the extension. During each live admission attempt, the powermetrics adapter exposes that attempt&#39;s rich CPU records in memory; the controller evaluates CPU/combined-power criteria before workload invoke, records the result in the existing <code>environment_admission.attempts</code> ledger, and retries/aborts or flags according to the base policy. Attempt selection is explicit, so the final admission decision and final CPU telemetry cannot be paired across retries. Current-mint attempt rows bind each measurement to a finite <code>start_s</code>/<code>end_s</code> wall-clock (epoch) window; the ordered ledger must be strictly increasing and non-overlapping (<code>end_i &lt;= start_(i+1)</code>). Missing or malformed timing refuses current claims, while frozen replay semantics remain unchanged. Because the windows are wall-clock, a backwards clock step between attempts mints an out-of-order ledger that strict validation permanently refuses — a fail-closed false refusal, never an admission; re-run the campaign member if this occurs. Missing adapter telemetry fails closed on live clocks; <code>FakeClock</code> fixture runs retain the pre-hookup GPU decision and record <code>cpu_admission_enforced: false</code> alongside the named missing-telemetry result. That field is an unconditional claim barrier in reducers/extraction; it is never evidence that GPU-only admission was scientifically sufficient. Live guard observations opt in to adapter-power capture, including a mandatory post-workload observation for every member. A missing post sample is unknown wattage (and therefore a production refusal), so renegotiation during the final workload cannot be hidden by an earlier clean sample.</p> <p>At window end, chain scripts can run:</p> <pre><code class="language-sh">python3 scripts/run_campaign.py --whole-window-verdict \

docs/process_traces/2026-08-07-night-hardening/AUDIT-MINT.md:4067:./docs/reviews/2026-07-08-technical-merit-review.md:58:Honestly routine: **Q5** (rank stability is standard benchmark-robustness work; the MDE-gated "unresolved tie" discipline is the contribution, not the answer), **Q3** (an analysis product of Q1/Q2's dataset, though at consumer links *both* the energy and latency axes of PD disaggregation are uncharacterized -- the correct charge is "no independent experiment," not "latency already done"), and the **affine-ladder energy-per-correct headline**, which is near-mechanical conditional on its envelope gate and on level-invariant per-item energy -- both empirical premises -- rather than scientifically central. The AP-5 C5-1.9 MoE-vs-dense energy-per-correct question is not tautological and should not be collapsed into that verdict. The scientifically interesting endpoint -- level-dependent per-item energy at fixed envelope -- is already the analysis plan's primary but should be the stated hypothesis. The measured 122B-vs-1.5B contrast carries essentially zero standalone weight (four-way confounded, n=3), and the project formally demoted it itself.

<!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>JouleWise Task Queue</h1> <p>This is the live queue for JouleWise work. When the user gives a new task, first triage it here instead of assuming it should happen immediately.</p> <h2 id="intake-rule-for-new-tasks">Intake Rule For New Tasks</h2> <p>For every new user task:</p> <ol> <li>Read <code>RUN_STATE.md</code>.</li> <li>Read this file.</li> <li>Check <code>git status --short --branch</code>.</li> <li>Review the last 2-3 commits with <code>git log --oneline --decorate -3</code>.</li> <li>Check relevant handoffs in <code>docs/run_reports/</code>.</li> <li>If <code>RUN_STATE.md</code> contains an ACTIVE <code>ACTIVE_STOP_CARD</code>, that card outranks this queue. Execute or preserve the card&#39;s resume/cleanup instructions before considering any lower-ranked work.</li> <li>Decide whether the task is:<ul> <li>urgent workspace hygiene,</li> <li>Phase 1 evidence work,</li> <li>Phase 2 implementation prep,</li> <li>later-phase research work,</li> <li>documentation/reporting,</li> <li>or unrelated/new scope.</li> </ul> </li> <li>Place or update the task in the queue with priority, rationale, evidence, and blockers.</li> <li>If executing it now, say why it outranks the current top task.</li> <li>Closure rule (D-023): a row may move to Completed only after the corresponding phase exit-checklist matrix row already shows the same status with dated evidence, and the Completed row&#39;s evidence cell must cite that matrix row (file + item id). If no matrix row exists for the work, say so explicitly in the evidence cell.</li> </ol> <h2 id="priority-scale">Priority Scale</h2> <ul> <li><strong>P0 Safety</strong>: prevents accidental data loss, bad commits, broken handoffs, or corrupted repo state.</li> <li><strong>P1 Phase Gate</strong>: required to close the current phase or unblock the next phase responsibly.</li> <li><strong>P2 Next Slice</strong>: next implementation slice after current phase gates are adequately planned or closed.</li> <li><strong>P3 Research Expansion</strong>: useful experiment or feature, but not needed for current gate.</li> <li><strong>P4 Polish</strong>: quality-of-life, dashboard polish, formatting, cleanup, or presentation work.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ranking-factors">Ranking Factors</h2> <p>Rank higher when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Prevents accidental loss or bad Git history.</li> <li>Produces evidence for the current phase exit checklist.</li> <li>Removes ambiguity for multiple later steps.</li> <li>Is required before physical hardware time is spent.</li> <li>Is cheap to verify and reduces future confusion.</li> <li>Matches the current phase better than jumping ahead.</li> </ul> <p>Rank lower when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Depends on unavailable hardware or supervisor input.</li> <li>Is a later-phase feature.</li> <li>Adds polish before a runnable vertical slice exists.</li> <li>Produces code without a clear run-bundle or test artifact.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ready-shelf-rule">Ready/Shelf Rule</h2> <p>A partially built or proposed task is <strong>READY</strong> only when it has:</p> <ul> <li>one authority document or stream-log pointer,</li> <li>bounded files/modules or a bounded artifact target,</li> <li>explicit acceptance evidence or a verification command,</li> <li>no hidden hardware/user/token-budget dependency, and</li> <li>a named lane (<code>[AGENT]</code>, <code>[QUIET-MAC]</code>, or <code>[ED-EXTERNAL]</code>).</li> </ul> <p>If any of those are missing, keep the item as a shelved concept or planning note instead of letting it compete with executable queue work. Half-finished work should be resumed only through its authority pointer and stop-card/checkpoint state, not by inference from prose summaries.</p> <h2 id="machine-state-lanes-adopted-c-007-2026-07-07">Machine-State Lanes (adopted C-007, 2026-07-07)</h2> <p>Every task carries a lane; a session picks the top task COMPATIBLE with its machine state, not the top task absolutely:</p> <ul> <li><strong>[QUIET-MAC]</strong> — measurement campaigns only: no agent fleet, no Codex load, idle gate will flag contamination.</li> <li><strong>[AGENT]</strong> — code, docs, feasibility spikes; safe during agent-heavy sessions.</li> <li><strong>[ED-EXTERNAL]</strong> — needs the user: advisor, calendar, device access, purchases, destinations.</li> </ul> <h2 id="historical-queue-snapshot-superseded-2026-07-15">Historical Queue Snapshot (superseded 2026-07-15)</h2> <p>The former hand-authored live table was removed because it duplicated kernel tasks. Dated completion and disposition history remains below; the generated Current Queue region is the sole live work-selection view.</p> <h2 id="completed-queue-items">Completed Queue Items</h2> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>ID</th> <th>Priority</th> <th>Completed</th> <th>Task</th> <th>Evidence</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>CODEX-BRIDGE-PET</td> <td>P4 Polish</td> <td>2026-07-18</td> <td>Make the native Codex pet reflect Claude Code background Sol work without changing adaptive effort routing</td> <td>No phase exit-checklist row exists for this personal bridge UI integration; <p>Living register of risks that could sink, delay, or weaken the capstone. Review at the start of every phase and whenever a trigger fires; update statuses at the end of substantial runs alongside <code>RUN_STATE.md</code>.</p> <p>Conventions:</p> <ul> <li>Likelihood/Impact: low / medium / high, judged against the current phase.</li> <li>Trigger: the observable event that means the risk is materializing.</li> <li>Mitigation: what we do <em>now</em> to reduce likelihood or impact.</li> <li>Fallback: what we do <em>if it happens</em> - every fallback must preserve a publishable result, even if smaller.</li> <li>Owner: <code>user</code> for actions needing
